title: One key shape for per-IP limits
evidence: The app routes key their per-IP limits on the /64 bucket (ipBucket in app-gate.server.ts; app-routes.server.ts, api.chat.ts web turns), while other per-IP limiters key on the address as read (api.feedback, api.events, api.measurements, api.google-token, api.lab-import-v2). Use one key shape for all. From the PR 1613 review. Design note docs/drafts/s-21-ip-key-design.md (owner rulings 2026-11-14; Brad's answer 2026-11-26). PR 1a of the series (1665): address keys normalised before use, the shape of the forwarded header counted (numbers only), an over-limit quota charge refused before it touches the map (US-52 AC4g-AC4i). PR 1b (1667): the forwarded hop read only where Fly writes its entry (AC4j), merging after the count is read. Verify at batch end: a normal storefront chat and lab upload are not refused; the 429 rate on those routes does not jump; the hourly forwarded-shape line appears in the logs. PR 2 (2082, US-52 AC4k): every per-IP limit builds its key with the one helper, clientKey(request, trust) in app/lib/ip-key.server.ts (ipBucket moved there from app-gate.server.ts): feedback, events, email capture, lab upload files, google token, reminders requests and opt-in (hashed bucket), guest sessions (hashed bucket; the session stays bound to the address, owner ruling 2a), mcp authorize, mcp rate-limit events (scopedKey per reason), mcp reviewer failures. mcp token stays on the address (owner ruling 1b), through allowTokenFrom in mcp-grants.server.ts. Per-kind limits (Brad 2026-11-26): perKindLimit in ip-key.server.ts gives an IPv6 /64 feedback 10 an hour (IPv4 and unknown 3) and new guest sessions 30 an hour (IPv4 and unknown 10); every other count and window unchanged; which header is trusted did not change. Left: PR 1b (1667, AC4j) and S-21b
durability_check: Every limiter states its key type: IpKey (made only in ip-key.server.ts) or PlainKey (which an IpKey cannot reach); the factories default to never. app/lib/ip-key.guard.test.ts fails on a getClientIp call outside the named list, an IpKey cast outside the helper, a limiter with neither type, a factory default other than never, or an address key joined into a string by a template or +
